cues.en: So when you originally started talking, you mentioned that you're going to address the why of going to Mars, but you never actually mentioned anything about that in your talk. Could you go over that? Sure. OK. As I see it, there's three reasons why Mars should be the goal of our space program. And in short, it's because Mars is where the science is, it's where the challenge is, and it's where the future is. It's where the science is because Mars
cues.zh: 你一开始发言时提到，你会讲为什么要去火星，但演讲里其实一直没提这件事。能展开说说吗？当然。好。在我看来，火星应该成为我们太空计划的目标，有三个原因。简而言之，因为火星是科学之所在，是挑战之所在，也是未来之所在。火星是科学之所在，因为火星

cues.en: OK, it was once a warm and wet planet. It had liquid water on its surface for more than a billion years, which is about five times as long as it took life to appear on Earth after there was liquid water here. So if the theory is correct that life is a natural development from chemistry, or if you have liquid water of various elements in sufficient time, life should have appeared on Mars, even if it subsequently went extinct. And if we can go to Mars and find fossils of past life, we'll have proven the development of life is a general phenomenon in the universe.
cues.zh: 好吧，它曾经是一颗温暖湿润的星球。它的表面有液态水超过十亿年，大约是地球上有液态水后生命出现所需时间的五倍。所以，如果生命是化学自然发展的理论正确，或者说，只要有液态水、各种元素和足够的时间，火星上就应该出现过生命，即使后来灭绝了。如果我们能去火星并找到过去生命的化石，就能证明生命的产生是宇宙中的普遍现象。

cues.en: Alternatively, if we go to Mars and find plenty of evidence of past bodies of water, but no evidence of fossils of the development of life, that could say that the development of life from chemistry is not sort of a natural process that occurs with high probability, but includes elements of free chance that we could be alone in the universe. Furthermore, if we can go to Mars and drill...
cues.zh: 另一种可能是，如果我们前往火星，发现大量过去存在水体的证据，却没有生命演化过程的化石证据，那可能说明从化学物质演化出生命并非一种高概率发生的自然过程，而是包含偶然因素，因此我们可能在宇宙中是孤独的。此外，如果我们能去火星并钻探……

cues.en: Because there's liquid water underground on Mars, reach the groundwater, there could be life there now. And if we can get hold of that and look at it and examine its biological structure and biochemistry, we could find out if life as it exists on Mars is the same as Earth life. Because all Earth life at the biochemical level is the same. We all use the same amino acids, the same method of replicating and transmitting information, RNA, DNA, all that. Is that what life has to be?
cues.zh: 因为火星地下有液态水，只要抵达地下水层，那里现在就可能存在生命。如果我们能取得样本，观察它、研究它的生物结构和生物化学，就能弄清火星上的生命是否与地球生命相同。因为在生化层面上，所有地球生命都是一样的：我们都使用相同的氨基酸、相同的复制与传递信息的方式——RNA、DNA 等等。那么，生命就非得是这个样子吗？

cues.en: Or could life be very different from that? Are we what life is, or are we just one example drawn from a much faster tapestry of possibilities? This is real science. This is fundamental questions that thinking men and women have wondered about for thousands of years, the role of life in the universe. This is very different from going to the moon and dating craters in order to produce enough data to get a credible paper to publish in the Journal of Geophysical Research and get tenure.
cues.zh: 又或者，生命可能与此截然不同？我们是生命的全部，还是只是从一幅更宏大的可能性织锦中抽出的一个样本？这是真正的科学，是根本性的问题——千百年来，善于思考的人们一直在思索生命在宇宙中的角色。这和登月、给陨石坑断代完全是两回事——那种做法是为了攒够数据、发出一篇能刊登在《地球物理研究杂志》上的靠谱论文，好拿到终身教职。

cues.en: you know, hypothesis-driven critical science. This is the real thing. Second, the challenge, okay? You know, I think societies are like individuals. We grow and we challenge ourselves. We stagnate when we do not. The humans to Mars program will be a tremendously bracing challenge for our society, be tremendously productive, particularly among youth, okay?
cues.zh: 你知道，假说驱动的批判性科学。这才是真格的。第二，挑战，对吧？你知道，我认为社会就像个体。我们会成长，也会挑战自我；不这么做就会停滞。人类登陆火星计划将是对我们社会极具振奋作用的挑战，也会极富成效，尤其在年轻人中，对吧？

cues.en: Humans to Mars program would say to every kid in school today, learn your science and you could be an explorer of a new world. We get millions of scientists, engineers, inventors, technological entrepreneurs, doctors, medical researchers out of that. And the intellectual capital from that would enormously benefit us. It would dwarf the cost of the program. And then finally, it's the future. Mars is the closest planet that has on it all the resources needed to support life and therefore civilization. If we do what we can do in our time to establish that little Plymouth Rock
cues.zh: 火星人类计划会对今天学校里的每个孩子说：学好科学，你就能成为新世界的探索者。我们会由此培养出数百万的科学家、工程师、发明家、科技创业者、医生和医学研究人员。由此产生的智力资本将极大地造福我们，远超该计划的成本。最后，这就是未来。火星是最近的一颗拥有维持生命乃至文明所需全部资源的行星。如果我们在这代人力所能及地建立那个小小的普利茅斯岩

cues.en: settlement on Mars. Then, 500 years from now, there'll be new branches of human civilization on Mars, and I believe, throughout nearby interstellar space. But, you know, look, I ask any American, what happened in 1492? They'll tell me, well, Columbus sailed in 1492, and that is correct. He did.
cues.zh: 火星定居点。然后，500年后，火星上将出现人类文明的新分支，而且我相信，还会遍布附近的星际空间。但你知道，你看，我问任何美国人，1492年发生了什么？他们会告诉我，嗯，哥伦布在1492年航行，这没错。他确实这么做了。

cues.en: But that's not the only thing that happened in 1492. In 1492, England and France signed a peace treaty. In 1492, the Borgias took over the Papacy. In 1492, Lorenzo de Medici, the richest man in the world, died. A lot of things happened. If there had been newspapers in 1492, which they weren't, but if they had, those would have been the headlines, not this Italian weaver son taking a bunch of ships and sailing off to nowhere. But Columbus is what we remember, not the Borgias taking over the Papacy.
cues.zh: 但1492年发生的并不只有那件事。1492年，英格兰和法国签署了和平条约。1492年，波吉亚家族掌控了教宗之位。1492年，世界首富洛伦佐·德·美第奇去世。发生了很多事。如果1492年有报纸——当时并没有——但如果有，那些才会是头条，而不是这个意大利织工的儿子带着一队船驶向无名之地。但我们记住的是哥伦布，而不是波吉亚家族掌控教宗之位。

cues.en: Well, 500 years from now, people are not going to remember which faction came out on top in Iraq, or Syria, or whatever, and who was in and who was out. But they will remember what we do to make their civilization possible. So this is the most important thing we could do.
cues.zh: 好吧，500年后，人们不会记得在伊拉克、叙利亚或其他地方哪个派系占了上风，谁上台谁下台。但他们会记得我们做了什么，让他们的文明成为可能。所以这是我们能做的最重要的事。

cues.en: the most important thing we could do in this time. And if you have it in your power to do something great and important and wonderful then you should.
cues.zh: 我们这个时代能做的最重要的事。如果你有能力去做伟大、重要而美好的事，那你就应该去做。
